hypotheses.justification: hlen is used only in `have hi' : i < next.length := by omega`, where i < (C.stepOfL Δ).length comes from `hS.nonBasicStep`. The same fact follows from the other hypotheses. Since `hi : i < (C.stepOfL Δ).length`, `hlab i hi` gives `C.Q.labelAt (x ++ [i]) = some _`. `labelAt q y` is `(q.atOpt y).map label` (QuasiTableau.lean:298), so `C.Q.atOpt (x ++ [i])` is `some _`. By `QuasiTab.atOpt_snoc` (PreInterpolant.lean:202), `atOpt (x ++ [i]) = (atOpt x).bind (fun n => n.children[i]?)`. With `hx` and `QuasiTab.children (QNode _ _ next) = next`, this is `next[i]?`. That is `some _` only if `i < next.length`. A proof: `by_contra hge; have hl := hlab i hi; unfold QuasiTab.labelAt at hl; rw [QuasiTab.atOpt_snoc, hx] at hl; simp [QuasiTab.children, List.getElem?_eq_none (by omega : next.length ≤ i)] at hl`. Nothing else in the statement mentions hlen. The theorem therefore stays true and provable without it, with the rest of the proof unchanged.
